text: Confirmed quota-aware batched runs specification v1.1; historical recovery fixture preparation authorized, runtime implementation not authorized.
Finish one fixed task-count times K experiment across arbitrarily sized invocations without repeating parameters or duplicating accepted slots.
Avoid further agent calls after explicit quota exhaustion without cancelling already running valid work.
Preserve reproducibility and honest measurement while reopening quota-interrupted logical trials, including identified historical runs.
No automatic waiting or scheduling until reset or inferred four/five-hour allowance; the operator manually initiates later batches.
No automatic sign-in, model/provider fallback, or account-wide quota coordination across unrelated runs.
Do not increase K/N between batches or retry ordinary failed tests until they pass.
Do not replace missing billed costs with API estimates or missing token counts with guesses.
Do not make smoke/prebuild batch commands, change benchmark task payloads, or alter DeepSWE history as part of this feature.

Runtime implementation and launching agents require separate authorization. The later fixture-preparation instruction authorizes only the documented Opus/Sol historical cleanup and dependent analytics withdrawal before code changes.

Preserve existing credential/container/network/redaction boundaries. Keep deletion and control records secret-free and limit deletion to resolved payload paths owned by the selected execution, never broad wildcard/run-root/unrelated cleanup.

Use focused existing build/tests and synthetic provider fixtures; tests must not mutate pinned tasks or real retained evidence or consume paid model quota. Existing CLI/Docker packaging and tmux operational guidance remain applicable.

Extend run with -b/--batch-size using existing recovery, rather than introduce a separate batch command. Govern the actual RunService parallel path, not only the standalone DeterministicScheduler; document initial, current-directory, and explicit-run-path examples.

The user rejected archival of quota-interrupted raw execution payloads and chose permanent deletion, after the durable secret-free audit/control prerequisite; passing partial patches are still invalid.

Historical migration is in scope for later authorized implementation. Archival of the already-published superseded Sol analytics snapshot is approved separately and does not permit retaining raw rejected agent payloads.
Keep task selection, checksums, K and logical-attempt identities unchanged across batches; completion means task-count times K terminal slots, including normal failed trials.

Persist a versioned batch record with identity, requested B, selected/admitted slot IDs and counts, timestamps, accepted/pending counts, stop reason, provider reset information when supplied and rejection references.

Before permanently deleting quota-interrupted payloads, persist rejection/pending control state and a minimal durable secret-free .github/tracking/ audit record: run K/N/P, provider/model/effort/CLI version and available commit identity, logical slot, outcome/error reason, available aggregate telemetry/known cost/time, affected paths and diagnosis. Mark missing values unknown.

Permanently delete only quota-interrupted execution payloads: raw logs, trajectory, partial patch, workspace and associated verifier payload/accepted terminal marker. Retain no raw copies in archive/retry paths; do not delete the immutable plan, batch/audit control records, unrelated slots or unrelated execution history.

Finalization and audit-before-delete are crash-safe and idempotent. Explicitly surface audit/deletion failures and block successful invalidation; interrupted cleanup remains recoverable without accepting a quota patch, duplicating terminal results or losing logical identity.

Keep known consumed cost/time from rejected executions separately observable from accepted-result metrics. Missing measurements stay null; rejected executions and retries never become additional logical trials.
Add run -b B with --batch-size B alias, reusing existing run/recovery behavior rather than adding a batch command. Batching also supports Copilot.

run --run-directory PATH -b B selects that exact run. Without a path, run -b continues only a valid retained run in the current directory; otherwise use ordinary new-run creation. Never discover nearby/latest runs. Recognizable corrupt run metadata fails rather than creating a different experiment.

Without -b preserve existing ordinary run/resume routing and supported overrides; ordinary run must not silently resume based on its directory. Claude/Codex quota stopping still applies as specified in REQ-017.

B limits distinct pending logical attempts admitted by the invocation, not successful outcomes, unique tasks, K waves or concurrency. Distinct logical slots starting agents cannot exceed B even when retained N exceeds B; ordinary retries remain inside their admitted slot.
Preserve existing attempt-wave/duration ordering across batches. When B exceeds pending work run only the remainder. Do not admit replacement slots for quota-interrupted work in the same batch.

Existing bounded infrastructure/verifier retries belong to their admitted logical slot and consume no additional B slot. Quota-interrupted slots wait for a later invocation with a new B budget, never automatic same-batch retry.

Require positive integer B; reject zero, negative, malformed and overflowing values before state/output-directory/resource mutation. Explicitly reject missing/invalid run paths, corrupt or inconsistent policy, checksum mismatches and conflicting continuation flags.
A completed run admits no work and exits successfully. A partially completed plan is not a completed run merely because its batch ends.
Dry-run reports exact selected IDs, admitted budget and remaining count without archive/deletion/state/output-directory/Docker/network mutation, for both current-directory and explicit-path forms.

Distinguish completed run, batch limit reached, quota pause, external cancellation and actual failure. Report requested/admitted/started/accepted/pending work and rejected quota executions distinctly. Normal batch completion/no work exits 0; quota pause has a distinct nonzero code selected during implementation research.

For Claude/Codex, the first observed explicit account/credit/usage-limit exhaustion or reset signal closes run-scoped agent admission on new runs and resumes with or without -b. Retain secret-free reason and supplied reset information without guessing timezone.

After the quota latch closes, start no new agent invocation or automatic agent retry, including work still preparing; such work stays pending. Starts already committed before latch closure are in-flight work.

Drain already running agents/verifiers, retain their valid results and reject each execution that independently reports quota. Do not cancel unrelated runs or invalidate other valid work because quota was hit.

Do not classify every HTTP 429, model-catalog refresh failure, network error, generic nonzero exit or transient service capacity error as account quota exhaustion; preserve their existing bounded retry/failure policy.

Allow one writer per retained run; concurrent batch/resume writers fail before admission while read-only status and dry-run remain available. Crash recovery preserves accepted results and recovers unfinished work without duplicate accepted terminal markers.

A quota-interrupted execution is invalid even if its partial patch passed verification. Permanently delete its payload after durable audit, keep the same logical slot pending and use a pristine workspace with the pinned CLI in a later batch.

Without recognized quota, missing token/billing usage produces a warning/null measurement, not automatic reopening. Ordinary failed tests and non-quota terminal outcomes keep existing policy; do not selectively rerun until passing.

Keep task-count times K planned slots as the scoring universe; pending slots do not shrink the denominator and rejected executions/retries do not add trials. Never present an incomplete 42-slot snapshot as a completed 56-slot run or substitute API estimates for billed costs.

Provide explicit dry-runnable/idempotent migration for wharf-swe/jobs/codex-gpt-6.1-sol-default-0.169.0/all-1. Audit and permanently delete/reopen exactly 14 quota slots: wharf-agent attempts 2/3/4; wharf-audit 1/2; wharf-host-profile 1; wharf-image-pull 1/4; wharf-reporting 2; wharf-scheduler 3; wharf-smoke 4; wharf-verifier 1/2/3. Keep 40 other passes and two failures terminal: 42 terminal/14 pending of 56.

Keep wharf-swe/jobs/claude-claude-opus-5-5-default-2.1.326/all-1 at 47 terminal/nine pending, but permanently delete the nine pending quota payloads after durable audit under the later fixture amendment. Preserve prior retry/cost/timing metadata in the audit, not raw payload copies. Keep its other 47 slots, immutable plan and append-only log unchanged. Do not blanket-delete nonzero exits or mutate unrelated arms/DeepSWE; later batches can continue the nine pristine pending slots.

During Sol migration retain the superseded exported analytics snapshot outside active data/*.jsonl discovery, withdraw the incomplete arm from the completed manifest/README comparison and canonically re-export/rebuild WharfSWE analytics only after all 56 slots finish. Snapshot retention does not permit keeping rejected raw agent payloads.

Continuing batches restore task subset/checksums, provider, exact effective CLI version, model, effort, K/N/P, ordering, timeouts, retry policy and other run settings. Only B and diagnostic/read-only controls vary; reject conflicting overrides and prevent ambient policy defaults replacing retained values. Never resolve a newer CLI.
Refresh credentials through existing provider locations, validate before resource preparation and never persist credential values. Rebuild missing images only for the same pinned CLI identity.

Unsupported legacy, malformed or mismatched retained metadata fails read-only unless explicitly migrated; batch continuation must not guess new policy. Preserve existing non-batch resume compatibility.

For 14 tasks/K=4, consecutive budgets 25,20,1,2,25 without interruption admit 25,20,1,2,8 slots and yield 56 unique terminal results with N>B and mixed passing/ordinary-failing outcomes. A sixth invocation admits zero and exits 0.
verification: Synthetic run across five budgets and a no-op sixth invocation; assert admitted IDs/counts, uniqueness, terminal failures and exit status.

text: Invalid B/path, conflicting flags, corrupt metadata and checksum mismatch fail before mutation. Current-directory and explicit-path continuations select identical pending IDs, never discover ancestors/latest runs and preserve legacy ordinary run/resume routing.
verification: Command-level positive/negative matrix with filesystem/resource snapshots and exact selected-ID assertions.

text: Inject quota with prepared, agent-running and verifier-running slots. No agent starts/retries after latch closure; in-flight work drains, valid results bank, prepared-only slots remain pending and the invocation reports quota pause with a distinct nonzero exit.
verification: Deterministic barrier-controlled concurrency test; compare start linearization events with stop latch and inspect terminal/pending states.

text: Explicit Claude/Codex quota signals stop admission with/without B and on resume; generic transient 429/network/catalog/capacity errors and missing-usage-only cases do not trigger quota invalidation.
verification: Synthetic provider event/error fixtures exercised through bounded/unbounded run and resume entry points.

text: Reject a quota patch even when tests pass. Verify durable secret-free audit/control records precede permanent payload deletion, no rejected raw copies remain, unrelated history is unchanged and the same slot later starts pristine with the exact pinned CLI.
verification: Synthetic passing-quota execution plus ordered audit/delete observations, scoped filesystem hashes and next-batch workspace/version assertions.

text: Crash/failure injection before/during deletion/finalization never loses audit, accepts a quota patch or duplicates terminal results; failures surface. A competing writer cannot admit work; read-only status/dry-run remain available without mutation or network activity.
verification: Failure-injected durable-state transitions and concurrent-writer/read-only integration checks.

text: Changed ambient model/version/concurrency defaults cannot alter continuing batch policy; refreshed credentials and B/diagnostic changes work without secret persistence or latest lookup. Policy overrides are rejected and missing pinned images retain exact CLI identity.
verification: Command/configuration integration matrix with mocked registry/provider calls, immutable policy snapshots and secret scanning of retained state.

text: Normal infrastructure/verifier retries consume one admitted slot; quota causes no same-batch replacement. A later batch selects the pending slot in preserved order; ordinary failed tests remain terminal.
verification: Synthetic retry/quota/ordinary-failure sequence with exact per-invocation admitted IDs and counts.

text: Migration dry-run selects exactly 14 documented Sol slots; execution yields 42 terminal/14 pending. Claude remains 47/9 but its nine authorized pending payloads are deleted after audit. Both plans/logs and all unrelated results remain unchanged; repeated migration is a no-op.
verification: Sanitized 56-slot fixture with exact affected IDs, scoped audit/deletion and idempotent second pass; real operational preparation separately authorized, never automatic test mutation.

text: Migration withdraws Sol's completed listing and retains its superseded export outside discovery. Interim denominator stays 56, not 42; completion permits canonical 56-row re-export. Rejected known spend/time stays separately visible and unknowns stay null.
verification: Synthetic migration/export/manifest/README reconciliation before and after slot completion, including null costs and rejected-spend totals.

verification: Replay versioned batch records for each outcome and assert console/status agreement and full-plan completion criteria.
